Theme

Latin word

facilis

facilis, facile

adjective, third declension; comparative facilior, superlative facillimus · Declension on Wiktionary

easy; easy to deal with, good-natured; good-natured, easy-going, affable

In this lexicon

  • easy

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Heaut. 1058–1059: ubi cognōris, facilia; Caes. BG 1.6.2: iter multō facilius atque expedītius (Lewis & Short); Traupman 184: Simplex est, it is simple

  • easy-going

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 152, 153; Cic. Fam. 5.2.9: lēnis et facilis (Lewis & Short); Traupman 308

  • kind

    also used · classical · Ter. Hec. 5.1.35: facilis benevolusque (Lewis & Short); Cic. Balb. 36: cōmēs, benignī, facilēs, suāvēs hominēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 323

Examples

  • Haec dum incipiās gravia sunt, dumque ignōrēs: ubi cognōris, facilia.

    These things are hard while you are starting and don’t know them; once you know them, they are easy.Ter. Heaut. 1058–1059

    In the entry for easy

  • ‘facilia’ inquit ‘mē docē’. cui praeceptor ‘ista’ inquit ‘omnibus eadem sunt, aequē difficilia’

    ‘Teach me the easy things,’ he said; and his teacher said, ‘These are the same for everyone, and just as hard.’Sen. Ep. 91.17
